headline: Google launches Playground, an AI platform for games
dek: Games are built from text prompts with no coding, for US users 18 or older, per Google AI.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Games from a text prompt
body: Google launched Playground, an experimental platform for creating, playing and sharing custom games without writing code. Users describe the idea in a text prompt (Google AI).
Launch is limited to US users aged 18 or older. Creation access is tiered and rolls out gradually, based on each user's Google AI subscription plan (Google AI).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: From prompt to playable game
s3.body: Games run in the browser, so a finished draft can be tested right away (Google AI).

points.t: Users begin from a blank canvas, remix a starter prompt or get guided support while building (Google AI).
Physics, rules, characters or setting change by typing a request, with no code touched (Google AI).
A game can stay private, be sent by link or be published to the Explore community gallery (Google AI).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Lowering the barrier
body: Google says making games has been limited to people who know complex game engines (software used to build games). Playground aims to let anyone turn an idea into a playable game (Google AI).
Gallery games pass a safety screening aligned with Google's Community Guidelines, and users can report them. Explore uses ratings and play activity to surface popular games (Google AI).

stat.cap: minimum age for US launch users (Google AI)

items.t: A closed beta of the Unity Spark integration is coming, bringing 3D graphics and the Unity engine (Google AI).
Google gave no timeline for other countries or a lower minimum age (Google AI).
Google calls Playground an early experiment that will keep evolving with its community (Google AI).

caption.hook: Google launched Playground, an AI platform that builds custom games from text prompts with no coding.
body: Google says games built in Playground work on phone and laptop, and games in select genres already support leaderboards and multiplayer. With a Play Games profile, users can claim a handle, favorite games and follow other creators.

Google also plans a Unity Spark integration for creators who want to go further than Playground offers today. The company says games made with it will stay available to everyone using Playground, not only to users with access to the professional-grade tools.
Google describes the service as "an early experiment" and invites users to share games and feedback.
caption.cta: Save it for later and send it to someone following AI.
